note: Majority: Civil Code, first part (Law No. 15/72 of 29 July 1972), in the text WIPO Lex holds, Article 492: a minor is anyone under 21 full years. The Civil Code was amended in 2021 (the amended Penal and Civil Codes were published in the Official Journal, as Gabonmediatime reported on 22 September 2021); the amended text itself wasn't read (the Official Journal's 'codes en vigueur' page lists the Civil Code, but its file link returns 404). Two pieces from March 2026, after that reform, still put civil majority at 21 under Article 492: a contribution in GabonReview ('trop jeunes pour avoir atteint la majorité civile fixée à 21 ans') and a column by the President of the Port-Gentil children's court in Gabonmediatime. They are held as secondary sources confirming that the 1972 age stands. The Children's Code (Law No. 003/2018) protects children only to 18, which the form doesn't hold, and neither does emancipation. Work: not held. The Labour Code WIPO Lex holds (Law No. 3/94, Article 177: no child employed before 16 save a derogation by decree) was replaced by the Labour Code of 2021, which wasn't reached: the Official Journal's file for it returns 404, the labour ministry's pages (travail.gouv.ga) carry summaries without the text, and Droit-Afrique refuses this client. Service: not read; no Gabonese defence law was reached (defense.gouv.ga and sgg.gouv.ga didn't answer).
